```{python}
#| label: setup
from IPython.display import HTML
import pyreadstat
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
from IPython.display import HTML

pio.templates.default = "plotly_white"
TEAL, TEAL_LT, CHARCOAL = "#00695C", "#80CBC4", "#333333"

df, meta = pyreadstat.read_sav("data/case31-efcu.sav")
n = len(df)

def tidy_fig(fig, height=None):
    fig = fig.update_layout(
        margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
        font=dict(family="Arial", color=CHARCOAL, size=13),
        showlegend=fig.layout.showlegend,
    )
    if height:
        fig.update_layout(height=height)
    fig = fig.update_layout(autosize=True)
    return HTML(fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=False,
                            default_height="100%", default_width="100%",
                            config={"responsive": True, "displaylogo": False}))

# Employee attributes (1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree)
emp_items = {"q3": "Courteous", "q4": "Helpful", "q5": "Professional", "q6": "Available"}
emp = (df[list(emp_items)].mean().rename(index=emp_items)
         .reset_index().set_axis(["Attribute", "Average"], axis=1)
         .sort_values("Average"))

# Credit union statements (1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree)
cu_items = {"q31": "Keeps accounts confidential", "q32": "Is prompt",
            "q33": "Meets members' needs", "q34": "Loan applications are simple",
            "q30": "Rates are lower than others"}
cu = (df[list(cu_items)].mean().rename(index=cu_items)
        .reset_index().set_axis(["Statement", "Average"], axis=1)
        .sort_values("Average"))

# Overall rating (6 = No Opinion and blanks are left out)
overall_labels = {1: "Excellent", 2: "Good", 3: "Average", 4: "Poor", 5: "Very Poor"}
overall = (df["q37"].map(overall_labels).value_counts()
             .reindex(list(overall_labels.values()), fill_value=0)
             .reset_index().set_axis(["Rating", "Members"], axis=1))
rated = overall["Members"].sum()
pct_top2 = overall.loc[overall["Rating"].isin(["Excellent", "Good"]), "Members"].sum() / rated

emp_score = df["employeeperformance"].mean()
pct_loan = (df["q27"] == 1).mean()
```

## Row {height="400px"}

```{python}
#| title: "How members rate employees (average, 1 to 5)"
fig = px.bar(emp, x="Average", y="Attribute", orientation="h", text="Average",
             color_discrete_sequence=[TEAL])
fig = fig.update_traces(texttemplate="%{text:.2f}", textposition="outside")
fig = fig.update_xaxes(range=[1, 5.4], title="1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree")
fig = fig.update_yaxes(title=None)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: "How members see the credit union (average, 1 to 5)"
colors = [TEAL_LT if s == "Rates are lower than others" else TEAL for s in cu["Statement"]]
fig = px.bar(cu, x="Average", y="Statement", orientation="h", text="Average")
fig = fig.update_traces(marker_color=colors, texttemplate="%{text:.2f}", textposition="outside")
fig = fig.update_xaxes(range=[1, 5.4], title="1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree")
fig = fig.update_yaxes(title=None)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

## Row {height="400px"}

```{python}
#| title: "Overall rating of the credit union"
fig = px.bar(overall, x="Rating", y="Members", text="Members",
             color_discrete_sequence=[TEAL])
fig = fig.update_traces(textposition="outside")
fig = fig.update_yaxes(title="Members", range=[0, overall["Members"].max() * 1.2])
fig = fig.update_xaxes(title=None)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: "Headquarters members (dark) vs. other members (light)"
hq = (df.assign(Group=df["q38"].map({1: "Headquarters", 2: "Other location"}))
        .groupby("Group")[["employeeperformance", "q32", "q33", "q34"]].mean()
        .rename(columns={"employeeperformance": "Employee score",
                         "q32": "Prompt", "q33": "Meets needs",
                         "q34": "Simple loan apps"})
        .reset_index()
        .melt(id_vars="Group", var_name="Measure", value_name="Average"))
fig = px.bar(hq, x="Measure", y="Average", color="Group", barmode="group",
             text="Average", color_discrete_sequence=[TEAL, TEAL_LT])
fig = fig.update_traces(texttemplate="%{text:.2f}", textposition="outside")
fig = fig.update_yaxes(range=[1, 5.2], title="Average (1 to 5)")
fig = fig.update_xaxes(title=None)
fig = fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

# Statements

## Row {height="460px"}

```{python}
#| title: "Is statement frequency right?"
freq_labels = {1: "Too Often", 2: "Very Often", 3: "About Right", 4: "Not Often Enough", 5: "Never"}
freq = (df["q9"].map(freq_labels).value_counts()
          .reset_index().set_axis(["Response", "Members"], axis=1))
fig = px.pie(freq, names="Response", values="Members", hole=0.55,
             color_discrete_sequence=[TEAL, TEAL_LT, "#B2DFDB"])
fig = fig.update_traces(textinfo="percent+label")
fig = fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: "How accurate are statements?"
acc_labels = {1: "Excellent", 2: "Good", 3: "Fair", 4: "Poor"}
acc = (df["q10"].map(acc_labels).value_counts()
         .reindex(list(acc_labels.values()), fill_value=0)
         .reset_index().set_axis(["Rating", "Members"], axis=1))
fig = px.bar(acc, x="Rating", y="Members", text="Members", color_discrete_sequence=[TEAL])
fig = fig.update_traces(textposition="outside")
fig = fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, acc["Members"].max() * 1.2])
fig = fig.update_xaxes(title=None)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: "Are statements easy to understand?"
und = (df["q11"].map({1: "Yes", 2: "No"}).value_counts()
         .reset_index().set_axis(["Response", "Members"], axis=1))
fig = px.pie(und, names="Response", values="Members", hole=0.55,
             color_discrete_sequence=[TEAL, TEAL_LT])
fig = fig.update_traces(textinfo="percent+label")
fig = fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
tidy_fig(fig)
```

# Data

```{python}
#| title: "Survey responses used in this dashboard"
cols = {"q3": "Courteous", "q4": "Helpful", "q5": "Professional", "q6": "Available",
        "employeeperformance": "Employee score", "q30": "Lower rates",
        "q31": "Confidential", "q32": "Prompt", "q33": "Meets needs",
        "q34": "Simple loan apps", "q37": "Overall rating (1 = Excellent)",
        "q27": "Has loan (1 = Yes)", "q38": "Headquarters (1 = Yes)"}
HTML(df[list(cols)].rename(columns=cols).to_html(index=False, classes="table table-sm table-striped", float_format="{:.2f}".format, na_rep="No answer"))
```

```{python}
#| title: "About this data"
#| output: asis
print("""
**Source:** Case 31, an employee credit union (EFCU) member survey provided for this course, with 128 respondents.

**Scales:** Employee and credit union items use 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree. The employee score is the average of the four employee items.

**Left out on purpose:** Overall ratings of "No Opinion" and blank answers are excluded from the overall rating chart. The product awareness questions (Q13 to Q26) contain a third answer code that has no label in the data file, so they are not charted until that code can be confirmed.

**Why this data:** My CEP client data from Cal Poly Pomona's Collins College has not arrived yet, so this dashboard uses the course case data to show the same kind of survey reporting I will build for the CEP.
""")
```
